sprint_note: Introduces measurement catalog (static JSON + GET endpoint), atomic batch ingestion endpoint, Chronos skill adapter, sparkline redesign with time-proportional x-axis and full vertical range, series list row 4-column layout with min/max, and UI fixes for input styling and timestamp display.
summary: NumericSeries tracks typed numeric measurements. This sprint adds a measurement catalog as the semantic foundation, a batch ingestion endpoint, a Chronos skill adapter, a redesigned sparkline and list row layout, and fixes UI styling and timestamp display.

classification.why_application: All behavior is domain-specific: measurement types are defined for this app, batch logic uses app-owned series, Chronos mapping is application-specific, and UX changes are app-local.
non_goals: Changes to edit/delete measurement UI beyond what is needed for styling consistency
classification.not_platform: The measurement catalog and batch logic are meaningful only within NumericSeries. The Chronos adapter is a thin consumer of this app's own API — not a reusable platform service.

failure_modes: UNKNOWN_KEY: batch contains a key not in measurement_definitions.json (422)
MISSING_TIMESTAMP: batch entry is missing recorded_at (422)
INVALID_VALUE: measurement value is not a finite number (422)
INVALID_TIMESTAMP: recorded_at cannot be parsed as ISO-8601 (422)
SERIES_NOT_FOUND: batch key maps to no series in numeric_series.series (422 — distinct from 404 since key is catalog-valid but no series row exists)
CHRONOS_UNMAPPED: label/alias does not resolve to a catalog key (Chronos skill returns error, does not call API)
CHRONOS_AMBIGUOUS: label matches multiple aliases (Chronos skill returns error)

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/measurement-definitions
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all measurement definitions from the static catalog as a Dataset. Used by UI for series creation picker and by Chronos skill for key resolution.
exposed_surfaces.response_success: Dataset: object_type=measurement_definition, rows=[{id, key, label, unit, value_type, description}]

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/measurements/batch
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Atomically insert multiple measurements in one request. Each entry references a catalog key (not a label_id). Resolves key → series via label_name=key lookup. All entries succeed or none are inserted.
exposed_surfaces.request_body: {recorded_at: ISO-8601 string, measurements: [{key: string, value: float}]}
exposed_surfaces.response_error: ApiError (422 for validation/unknown key, 422 for no series found)
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: none — external Chronos integration and internal batch form

exposed_surfaces.name: 00_architecture/measurement_definitions.json
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Source of truth for all valid measurement types. Backend loads this at startup. Keys are canonical identifiers used in the batch API and series label names.

exposed_surfaces.name: Chronos NumericSeries adapter
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Thin Chronos skill that maps human label/alias input to catalog keys, constructs a batch request, and calls POST /api/measurements/batch. Does not contain business logic. Fails on unmapped or ambiguous input.

internal_flow.name: catalog_load
internal_flow.description: At service startup, measurement_definitions.json is loaded from 03_Application/NumericSeries/00_architecture/measurement_definitions.json into memory as a dict keyed by catalog key. This dict is used for key validation in batch ingestion and served as-is via GET /api/measurement-definitions. No database table is needed — the catalog is a versioned static artifact.
outputs: in-memory catalog dict: {key → {label, unit, value_type, description, aliases}}

internal_flow.name: catalog_endpoint
internal_flow.description: GET /api/measurement-definitions reads the in-memory catalog dict and returns all entries as a Dataset. Each entry is a row with id=key. Schema: id, key, label, unit, value_type, description. Rows ordered by label ASC.
outputs: Dataset (object_type=measurement_definition, rows sorted by label ASC)

internal_flow.name: batch_ingestion
internal_flow.description: POST /api/measurements/batch receives {recorded_at, measurements: [{key, value}]}. Steps: (1) validate recorded_at is valid ISO-8601 (reject 422 INVALID_TIMESTAMP if not). (2) For each entry: validate key is in catalog (reject 422 UNKNOWN_KEY if not); validate value is finite (reject 422 INVALID_VALUE if not). (3) Resolve each key to a label_id via: SELECT s.label_id FROM numeric_series.series s JOIN labels.labels l ON l.id = s.label_id WHERE lower(l.name) = lower(key). If any key has no series row, reject entire request 422 SERIES_NOT_FOUND. (4) Open a single transaction. Insert all measurements. Commit. Return 201 {inserted: N}. On any exception: rollback.
outputs: ApiError on any validation or lookup failure

internal_flow.name: sparkline_data
internal_flow.description: The list endpoint (GET /api/series) is extended to return, per series: sparkline_points (JSON-encoded array of {v: float, ts: int} where ts is Unix epoch milliseconds of recorded_at), min_value (float|null), max_value (float|null), latest_value (float|null). Sparkline window: 20 most recent measurements ordered by recorded_at ASC. The ts field enables time-proportional x-axis rendering on the frontend without any backend coordinate calculation. min and max are computed over ALL measurements for the series (not just the sparkline window).

internal_flow.name: timestamp_display
internal_flow.description: recorded_at values stored in Postgres as TIMESTAMPTZ are returned to the frontend as ISO-8601 strings (UTC). Frontend formats them for display: toLocaleString() with options {year:'numeric', month:'2-digit', day:'2-digit', hour:'2-digit', minute:'2-digit'} using the browser's local timezone. Time authority: client displays in local timezone; server stores in UTC. This is acceptable because recorded_at is a user-declared measurement time (not a server event time).
outputs: Human-readable local datetime string for display

internal_flow.name: datetime_input
internal_flow.description: For add/edit measurement forms, replace the single datetime-local input with two separate inputs: type=date (value=YYYY-MM-DD) and type=time (value=HH:MM). On submit, the frontend combines them with the browser's UTC offset to produce a timezone-aware ISO-8601 string: (1) combine as localStr = date + 'T' + time + ':00'; (2) compute the offset: const d = new Date(localStr); const off = -d.getTimezoneOffset(); const sign = off >= 0 ? '+' : '-'; const hh = String(Math.floor(Math.abs(off)/60)).padStart(2,'0'); const mm = String(Math.abs(off)%60).padStart(2,'0'); const tzStr = sign+hh+':'+mm; (3) send recorded_at = localStr + tzStr. Time authority: the user's local clock is the measurement time. The browser offset string makes this explicit. Postgres stores as TIMESTAMPTZ (converts to UTC internally). Display: formatted back to local timezone using toLocaleString(). This approach preserves the user's intent without relying on server timezone assumptions.

internal_flow.name: input_styling
internal_flow.description: All input elements in SeriesDetailPage (add measurement form, edit form) are updated to use CSS theme tokens: background → var(--md-sys-color-surface), border → 1px solid var(--md-sys-color-outline-variant), color → var(--md-sys-color-on-surface), border-radius → 4px. No hardcoded hex colors remain on form inputs. Table header and row borders also updated to use var(--md-sys-color-outline-variant).
outputs: updated inline styles on all input elements in SeriesDetailPage

internal_flow.name: list_row_layout
internal_flow.description: SeriesListPage row layout changes from 3 columns (label | sparkline | current) to 4 columns: label | sparkline | min/max | current. Grid template: '140px 1fr 70px 80px'. Min/max column shows min and max from all measurements, stacked vertically (min on bottom, max on top). Current value column shows latest_value. Empty states: if no measurements, all value columns show '—'. Sparkline redesign: frontend uses sparkline_points [{v, ts}] array. X positions are proportional to timestamp range (ts_min to ts_max mapped to 0%–100% of container width). Y positions are normalized: (v - min_value) / (max_value - min_value) * 100%. Edge cases: single point → render centered dot; identical values (min==max) → render midline; empty dataset → render '—' dash; identical timestamps → render as single point.
outputs: 4-column list row with custom SVG sparkline component

internal_flow.name: chronos_skill
internal_flow.description: The Chronos NumericSeries skill is a Python function (or Chronos tool definition) that: (1) Accepts {measurements: [{label: str, value: float}], recorded_at?: str}. (2) Loads measurement catalog (fetches GET /api/measurement-definitions or uses bundled snapshot). (3) For each input label: searches catalog entries (key, label, aliases) for a case-insensitive exact match. Fails with CHRONOS_UNMAPPED if no match. Fails with CHRONOS_AMBIGUOUS if multiple matches (should not happen with well-defined catalog). (4) Constructs batch request: {recorded_at: recorded_at or current UTC ISO-8601, measurements: [{key, value}]}. (5) Calls POST /api/measurements/batch. Returns success or error verbatim. Constraint: no business logic, no silent remapping, no invented keys.
inputs: recorded_at: str (optional, defaults to current UTC ISO-8601 if omitted)
outputs: CHRONOS_UNMAPPED error if label not found
CHRONOS_AMBIGUOUS error if label matches multiple entries
API error from batch endpoint verbatim

deferred_decisions: Whether series creation UI should present a catalog picker (select from definitions) or remain a free-text name input. Draft says 'series = measurement' (one series per measurement type) but does not mandate a picker UI. Implementer may use a picker that sets label_name=key, or keep the existing free-text input.

Whether Chronos skill fetches catalog live from GET /api/measurement-definitions or uses a bundled snapshot. Live fetch is more consistent but adds a network call. Implementer decides based on Chronos runtime constraints.

risks.risk: Recharts removal from SeriesListPage: if recharts is imported elsewhere in the component it must be retained as a dependency. Check all imports before removing.
risks.impact: Build failure if recharts import is removed but still used.

risks.risk: measurement_definitions.json loaded at startup: if file is missing or malformed, app fails to start. Implementer must add a clear startup error message.
risks.impact: Opaque startup failure without explicit error.

risks.risk: Split date+time input: browser UTC offset computation via getTimezoneOffset() returns the offset for the current moment. If a historical date is entered and DST changes apply, the offset may be incorrect by 1 hour.
risks.impact: Measurement time may be off by one hour for historical entries entered during a DST boundary. Acceptable for MVP — the user controls the value and can correct it.

risks.risk: Sparkline ts field: uses Unix epoch milliseconds (JavaScript Date.now() compatible). Backend must return as integer, not string.
risks.impact: Frontend time-proportional math fails if ts is a string.

open_questions.question: Should GET /api/series (list) continue to return sparkline_values (JSON float array) for backward compatibility with any consumer, or can the field be replaced entirely by sparkline_points [{v, ts}]?
open_questions.note: Recommendation: replace sparkline_values with sparkline_points. The only consumer is SeriesListPage which is being rewritten in this sprint.
